headline: Profit slides as Sun Pharma buyout advances toward close
summary_short: Organon's Q2 2026 revenue was $1,558M (+6.7% q/q, -2.3% y/y) and diluted EPS fell to $0.40 (-28.6% y/y) as margins compressed; the company's pending $14.00/share Sun Pharma acquisition, approved by stockholders in July, is expected to close in early 2027.
summary_long: Revenue fell 2.3% y/y to $1,558M (+6.7% q/q) as growth in Hadlima (+59%), Zetia/Vytorin (+16%), and Emgality (+27%) was offset by declines in Ontruzant (-81%), Singulair (-27%), and Nexplanon (-4%), the latter pressured by delayed reinsertions following the five-year label change. Gross profit fell 3% y/y to $847M on unfavorable volume, pricing, and mix. Net income dropped 25.5% y/y to $108M ($0.40 diluted EPS, -28.6% y/y) as SG&A and R&D both declined but were outweighed by the revenue and margin pressure. Cash rose to $1,132M (+89% y/y) after $433M of Jada divestiture proceeds. Organon's pending $14.00/share all-cash acquisition by Sun Pharma — stockholder-approved in July 2026 — is expected to close in early 2027.

drivers.explanation: Profitability declined across the board while Organon proceeds toward its previously announced $14.00/share all-cash acquisition by Sun Pharma, which received stockholder approval in July 2026 and is expected to close in early 2027.

Growth in Hadlima (+59%), Zetia/Vytorin (+16%), and Emgality (+27%) was more than offset by declines in Ontruzant (-81%), Singulair (-27%), and Nexplanon (-4%), the latter due to delayed reinsertions following the five-year label approval.
Gross profit fell due to unfavorable volume, pricing, and product mix, plus unfavorable foreign exchange, per the release's own discussion.
Lower gross profit and a $17M unfavorable Dermavant working-capital resolution outweighed reduced SG&A and R&D spend from restructuring initiatives.
EPS fell more steeply than net income (-28.6% vs -25.5% y/y) because diluted shares outstanding rose 3.9% y/y to 270.4M.
EBITDA declined in line with lower gross profit and operating income amid the same unfavorable volume, pricing, mix, and FX pressure.
Cash rose largely on $433M of proceeds from the January 2026 divestiture of the Jada System to Laborie.
Debt declined following the 2025 repurchase and cancellation of ~$419M of 5.125% notes and Q1 2026 mandatory term-loan prepayments.
